Shanghai/Ningbo.waitLabel: SNH 4-7 days · NGB 3-5 days (as of 12 Aug)
Shanghai/Ningbo.note: Terminals at Waigaoqiao, Yangshan and Ningbo-Zhoushan have been open since 10-11 Aug, so this is backlog rather than closure. The queue is not visibly clearing: Linerlytica's newest snapshot is still 16 Aug and shows 1.89m TEU at anchorage with a queue-to-berth ratio of 3.25, worst of the 18 tracked ports by a wide margin. Linerlytica has published nothing for six days, so those figures are stale rather than improving. Berth-wait figures are still SEKO's 12 Aug numbers (Shanghai 4-7 days, Ningbo 3-5 days); no source has published newer ones in ten days. Two systems are now in range: Tropical Storm Gaenari is 575 km to the south-east in the Taiwan Strait and moving away, but Typhoon Saudel's five-day track brings it to about 596 km east of the port group at 117 hours, inside the 600 km threat radius for the first time.
Shanghai/Ningbo.source: SEKO Asia-Pacific Logistics Monitoring Center, 12 Aug; Kuehne+Nagel port update, 18 Aug; JMA TC2621 and TC2623, 23 Aug JST

Xiamen.event: Tropical Storm Gaenari (Typhoon Saudel behind it)
Xiamen.note: Gaenari is in the Taiwan Strait tracking west-south-west and JMA's forecast puts it about 181 km from Xiamen at 45 hours, weakening to a tropical depression as it closes. Behind it, Typhoon Saudel is forecast to reach the northern entrance of the strait at 117 hours, roughly 452 km away and still at 65 kt. The China Meteorological Administration activated a Level IV emergency response on 22 Aug with heavy rain forecast for coastal Fujian through 24 Aug. No terminal has announced a suspension and no source has published a berth-waiting figure for Xiamen, so this is a forecast watch only.
Xiamen.source: JMA TC2623 and TC2621 specifications, 23 Aug JST; CGTN and Global Times, 22 Aug

Haiphong.note: Narra is sitting in the Gulf of Tonkin about 106 km from the port and JMA's track keeps it over the gulf for roughly two more days before it moves inland over Guangxi. Hai Phong deployed more than 11,000 personnel on 22 Aug and neighbouring Ninh Binh and Hung Yen imposed sea bans, but no source states that Hai Phong terminals themselves have suspended operations, so the status stays at watch. Over 500 mm of rain is forecast for parts of northern Vietnam.
Haiphong.source: JMA TC2622 specifications, 23 Aug JST; VietnamPlus, 22 Aug

Shenzhen (Yantian).note: Narra's closest approach to Yantian is about 516 km at 69 hours, just inside the threat radius, and the forecast track then takes it inland over Guangxi and away from the port. The threat is easing rather than building. Heavy rain is still forecast for Guangdong through 24 Aug under the CMA Level IV response. SEKO's last published figure, from 12 Aug, had South China gateways operating normally with 2-4 day vessel waits; nothing newer has been issued.
Shenzhen (Yantian).source: JMA TC2622 specifications, 23 Aug JST; SEKO Asia-Pacific Logistics Monitoring Center, 12 Aug; Global Times, 22 Aug

remarks: Four systems are active in the JMA feed and three of them sit near the China coast, which is why the CMA activated a Level IV typhoon and heavy-rain emergency response on 22 Aug.

Typhoon Saudel is the one to watch. It is the only genuine typhoon in the group, forecast to strengthen to 95 kt near Iwo Jima, pass Okinawa around Wednesday, and still be a 65 kt typhoon at the northern end of the Taiwan Strait in five days. That track ends about 596 km from Shanghai/Ningbo, which is already carrying the worst anchorage queue of any tracked port.

Tropical Storm Gaenari is the nearest-term risk. It is weakening as it crosses the Taiwan Strait toward Fujian and JMA has it down to a depression by 45 hours, so the likely effect at Xiamen is rain and pilotage disruption rather than a shutdown.
Narra is parked over the Gulf of Tonkin roughly 106 km from Haiphong and heading inland over Guangxi, so its effect on Yantian is fading rather than growing.

No port in the tracked set is currently suspended. No carrier or terminal has published a closure notice: MSC's newsroom carries nothing typhoon-related and SEKO's live page has not moved since 12 Aug.
Berth-waiting figures across the board are ten days old. Treat every reported wait in this file as a 12 Aug reading, not a current one.
Linerlytica has not published a congestion snapshot since 16 Aug, so the congestion panel is six days behind the weather panel.
